findings.issue: The negative check in the new published-helper import sensor misses the deep paths it is meant to reject. I ran its regex against sample specifiers. It returns false for '@stynx-nyx/testing/src/index', '@stynx-nyx/testing/src/fake-transaction', '../../../testing/src/index', '../../angular-auth/testing/index', '../../angular-auth/src/testing' and '../../../packages/testing/src/x'. It only matches when another path segment comes before '/src/', for example '@stynx-nyx/angular-auth/testing/src/index'. The positive check does hold: each of the ten adoption files imports its published specifier, and a hand review found no source-deep helper imports today. So this is a sensor weakness, not an actual violation.
findings.required_change: Inspector tightens the negative pattern. It should reject any '@stynx-nyx/<helper-pkg>/src/' specifier, any relative specifier that reaches '(testing|angular-auth|angular-i18n)/(src|testing)/', and any 'testing/index' helper path. Add self-test vectors for these cases. Architect rebinds trace.

findings.issue: The alias now points at packages/testing/src/index.ts, which fixes Transaction identity. That barrel also loads mint-test-session, which imports @stynx-nyx/sessions at runtime. @stynx-nyx/sessions resolves to its built CommonJS dist. Turbo neither orders sessions#build or testing inputs before data#test nor includes them in data#test cache inputs. In ci:stynx, `pnpm typecheck` runs before `pnpm test` and builds sessions, so the gate is sound. But an isolated `pnpm --filter @stynx-nyx/data test` on a clean tree can fail to resolve. A cached data#test result can also survive an edit to testing/src/fake-transaction.ts.
findings.required_change: Optional hardening, not needed for import. Either alias '@stynx-nyx/testing' to '../testing/src/fake-transaction.ts' for data unit tests, or declare the testing/src inputs for data#test in turbo. Do not add a manifest dependency.

findings.issue: The browser spec now tabs Home → Settings → collapse control, and from the collapse control → Theme. It also asserts the accessible names, aria-expanded and pt-BR 'Tema' after reload. findings.required_change: None required. If the reference header is reordered later, add an assertion that the first Tab from the start of the document reaches the skip link.

summary:
I reviewed HEAD 189b64bb against cycle-1 HEAD 4caa1e64 and predecessor e8931c57. All three cycle-1 blockers are repaired in test source and config, with no product-source change for them.

(1) System theme. packages-web/angular-ui/test/shell.spec.ts now has a StynxShellThemeService suite with a controllable matchMedia stub. It asserts the exact query. Dark resolves to 'dark', and change events flip the result to light and back while the preference is 'system'. An explicit 'dark' ignores changes both ways, persists, and reloads. An invalid stored value resolves from the current media state and reacts to changes. With matchMedia undefined the result is 'light'. With PLATFORM_ID 'server' it is 'light' and matchMedia is never called, even with a stored 'dark'. Denied storage keeps the in-memory preference. These cases match StynxShellThemeService in shell.component.ts.

(2) Live status. An it.each over en and pt-BR asserts the exact role=status text after router navigation ('Navigation changed to Settings' / 'Navegação alterada para Configurações'). It also asserts the text after selecting Dark ('Theme changed to Dark' / 'Tema alterado para Escuro'), plus the aria-label and that the menu closes. These strings match the published en.json and pt-BR.json catalogs.

(3) Data identity. vitest.config.ts and vitest.stryker.config.ts alias '@stynx-nyx/testing' to testing/src and keep '@stynx-nyx/data' → src. The data manifest still has no testing dependency, so there is no cycle. transaction.spec.ts asserts toBeInstanceOf(Transaction) on the fake and restores rejects.toBeInstanceOf(TransactionRequiredError) for execute and query after close.

Other items. No assertion was weakened: the old `not.toBe('system')` checks became exact values, and the status label follows the catalog. The browser spec adds keyboard traversal to the collapse and Theme controls and pt-BR persistence. The plan now records the CTG5 Transaction-fake inventory (only data/transaction.spec uses the concrete class; outbox uses the structural port) and declares roles for the ten human-authored commits. The SDK repair merges a sibling requestId into a legacy context only when that key is absent, with a Inspector red test before the Engineer fix. All repair commits use DEVAI role identities and touch disjoint paths.

I ran two gates myself: check:trace is ok at 442/442, and the new import sensor passes. Architect trace rebinds cover all five changed projections. Not re-run here: the IFM/NGERR/SHELL/TEST MUST proofs from cycle 1 (real Nest/PostgreSQL If-Match with TransactionalCommand composition, the 428/412 law envelopes and requestId, NGERR precedence, SSE bypass, provider parity, axe) and the error catalog and API baselines. They are unaffected by the repair diff, whose only product-source change is packages-web/sdk/src/errors.ts. All other gates are as reported by the maestro.

The remaining findings are sensor strength and test isolation hygiene only. This HEAD is safe for ordered import under OD-S15-02.
